screens.name: Home · Grid
screens.what: Dashboard → Home: title bar 40, sidebar 260, sort chip + grid/list toggle, quick cards, 3-up grid.
screens.note: The sort chip names the current order and the grid/list toggle is a real hit target; both were the messy part of this screen before the IA pass.

screens.name: Home · List
screens.what: The same files in the List layout: one panel, NAME / TEAM / EDITED header, rows 48 tall.
screens.note: NAME and EDITED are sortable — the header chevron marks the active key; clicking a header sorts, clicking the sort chip opens the same list.

screens.name: Recents
screens.what: Sidebar view: files touched recently, same grid and sort machinery.
screens.note: `visible_files()` is the one filter+sort list every view reads, so Recents cannot disagree with Home about order.

screens.name: Starred
screens.what: Starred files only; the star sits on the card and in the row.
screens.note: Starring is per file and shows in both layouts; the sort has a Starred-first mode that keeps recency inside each group.

screens.name: Trash (empty)
screens.what: Trash with nothing in it — an empty state with a way back.
screens.note: This used to be a dead end with no content and no exit; the state now says what Trash is for.

screens.name: Selection + sort menu
screens.what: Two files selected: bulk bar at the bottom, sort menu open over the grid.
screens.note: ⌘A selects everything visible, Esc unwinds menu → selection → focus ring. The bulk bar only exists while something is selected.

screens.name: No files yet
screens.what: An empty recents list (first run, or a search that matches nothing): instructions plus the two actions that get you out.
screens.note: The empty state offers "Open existing file"; with a file present the same slot shows the grid.

screens.name: Templates
screens.what: The template gallery modal: 48 audited starting points, one glyph per row.
screens.note: Backed by OpenDoc::TEMPLATES; a test asserts every row has a distinct glyph (a column of identical chips was the bug).

screens.name: Editor · Structure + canvas
screens.what: Full editor chrome: title bar 36, rail 48, left dock 280 (STRUCTURE / LIBRARY / TOKENS), right dock 340, rulers, tool dock 40 tall. The COMPOSE inspector is drawn from paint_design: name + %, W/H, X/Y, rotation, Auto layout, Flow, Resizing, Alignment, Padding, Clip content, Appearance, Typography — fields are filled boxes with no outline until hover, and the value being typed into is ringed.
screens.note: Three canvas aids ship in this frame: the minimap (bottom-right, ⇧M or its ✕), page sketches in every PAGES row that has content, and ⇧1 fitting the frame to the page content.

screens.name: Editor · Library
screens.what: Left dock on LIBRARY: assets in this file, then linked libraries.
screens.note: The left tabs are STRUCTURE / LIBRARY / TOKENS — X-Native names its own model (scene graph, not a Figma clone).

screens.name: Editor · Tokens
screens.what: Left dock on TOKENS: the document variables, grouped by kind.
screens.note: Variable edits route through the undo log; the inspector shows the variable name beside any bound fill.

screens.name: Editor · Flow (prototype)
screens.what: Right dock on FLOW: start point, interactions, animation; connections draw on the canvas.
screens.note: “▶ Preview flow start” enters the chrome-less flow viewer (next screen).

screens.name: Editor · Ship (inspect)
screens.what: Right dock on SHIP: size, fill (with its variable), text style, and the CSS line.
screens.note: The fill row names the variable it is bound to, which is the link the paint library edits.

screens.name: Editor · UX analysis
screens.what: Right dock on UX ANALYSIS: contrast, flow gaps, quality notes.
screens.note: The contrast rows read the same audited pairs the palette table and the CLI theme audit use.

screens.name: Paint library (new)
screens.what: The fill/stroke library popover: variables (active mode resolved, tick on the bound one), paint styles, and a detach row.
screens.note: Linking is by reference, not a copy: a bound row shows the variable name, the popover is 300 wide, lists ≤8 variables then "+N more in Variables (⌥5)", and Detach keeps the resolved colour.

screens.name: Guides + guide readout (new)
screens.what: Dragging a node: smart guides, ruler guides, and the mono readout chip that follows the pointer.
screens.note: The readout is clamped to the canvas and only exists inside it; the minimap and the page sketches are the other two aids from the same pass.

screens.name: Empty page (⇧1)
screens.what: A page with nothing on it: the canvas says what to do, and ⇧1 frames the camera instead of fitting nothing.
screens.note: Content-fit fits the union of visible nodes with 24 px of padding; on an empty page it falls back to framing the camera.

screens.name: Command palette (⌘K)
screens.what: Centred 480×400 palette: input 40 tall, rows 30, categories File→Help.
screens.note: Command-first discovery; fuzzy search over registered commands, ↑↓ to move, ⏎ to run.

screens.name: Context menu
screens.what: Right-click menu, 208 wide with 28-tall rows, keyboard hints on the right.
screens.note: The canvas menu carries the view toggles the last pass added — Toggle minimap (⇧M) sits beside Toggle grid.

screens.name: Colour picker
screens.what: The fill colour popover: hex, opacity, the accent ramp, and the palette note.
screens.note: Colour popovers are modal to the inspector: clicks inside are consumed, so a pick never falls through to the canvas.

screens.name: App menu
screens.what: The hamburger menu, 220 wide: file actions, export, find, theme, preferences.
screens.note: Every row here is a real action; shortcuts are shown only where the app binds them.

screens.name: Find & replace
screens.what: Find bar with replace row, match counter, case and selection-only toggles.
screens.note: ⇧⌘F opens it; matching is document-wide by default, or scoped to the selection.

screens.name: Notifications
screens.what: Toasts in the corner: what happened, and the shortcut that undoes it.
screens.note: The undo toast names the exact operation because "Undo" alone never tells you what you are undoing.

screens.name: Board
screens.what: Infinite canvas: header 36 with a way back, dot grid, sticky notes, links, board tool dock (9 tools), zoom chip, outline.
screens.note: Boards carry their own tool set and a Grid / Links toggle; the header keeps a visible route to the dashboard.

screens.name: Flow viewer (present)
screens.what: Prototype playback: no chrome at all, hit targets numbered, preview chip floating.
screens.note: The flow viewer hides the docks, rulers and toolbar so the prototype gets every pixel; the chip is the only chrome left.

screens.name: Document loading
screens.what: The loading screen: card, spinner, progress, and the nine phases named as they happen.
screens.note: Elapsed time changes the spinner, never the phase; a failure offers Recover / Open saved file, a working phase offers Cancel.
